source.title: The Lifecycle Principle: Stabilizing Dynamic Neural Networks with State Memory

record.file_problem: The supplied text contains the full paper, though some table entries appear garbled or inconsistent in the flattened rendering.
record.tranche_reason: The paper compares its own regularization intervention and reports test accuracy and proposed generalization proxies, but it does not test the listed claim versions directly. Its regularization results concern held-out performance, not the training–test gap or the versions' specific interventions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports test accuracy, corruption accuracy, calibration, Hessian top eigenvalue, and Lipschitz-bound proxy for LCL and comparators. Those results do not measure the specific behaviors named by V1–V8: no random-label memorization, width sweep, convolution-versus-fully-connected comparison, optimizer comparison, batch-size comparison, dropout-specific generalization result, magnitude-aware sharpness measure, or removal of memorized examples. These are not rows for the listed versions.
record.test_reason: Tables 1–3 directly compare Dropout with a no-added-regularizer baseline on held-out accuracy, testing V6 in additional architectures and training settings. Testing training-set size or dropout strength is not necessary to test this part of V6. The record incorrectly excludes these comparisons.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately paraphrases the author's conclusion: LCL improves generalization and robustness, state memory is critical, and smoothing and capacity reduction are proposed explanations. These are the author's claims; the tables show exceptions, including lower CIFAR-100 corruption accuracy with LCL for all three architectures and higher Hessian eigenvalues in several settings.
record.recipe_differences: Lifecycle Linear deactivates neurons for sampled periods, stores their parameters, and restores them on revival; the study compares it with standard baselines and regularizers. It does not reproduce a listed version's method.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper varies architecture and dataset in its LCL experiments, but these comparisons do not test a listed claim version.

fits_no_version.finding: LCL and its ablations change clean accuracy, corruption accuracy, and calibration across architectures and datasets.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Long-term neuron deactivation with parameter restoration can affect classification performance and robustness.

fits_no_version.finding: The study reports Hessian top eigenvalues and products of spectral norms, without magnitude-aware perturbation measurements or empirical training–test gaps.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: LCL changes curvature and spectral-norm proxies; these measurements do not test V7.

fits_no_version.finding: DeiT-Tiny Dropout accuracy is 82.21% versus 82.28% baseline on CIFAR-10 and 53.59% versus 54.01% on CIFAR-100.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Dropout does not improve mean test accuracy in these vision-transformer training configurations.

record.problems: The supplied table rendering includes malformed or ambiguous entries, including an apparent duplicate LCL-no-warmup row in Tables 1 and 2 and corrupted scientific-notation values. The paper reports means with ± values but does not identify what those uncertainty values represent in the supplied text. No training-error or generalization-gap measurements are reported.
record.rows_left_out: No rows kept: the reported outcomes do not measure what any V1–V8 names. Table 1, Table 2, Table 3, and the theoretical-analysis discussion report test accuracy and proxy metrics, not the specified claim-version behaviors.

Width sweep beyond interpolation threshold and resulting test error.

relationships.condition: ResNet-18 and EfficientNetV2-S trained from scratch on augmented CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100
relationships.reason: Tables 1–2 show only a small ResNet-18 CIFAR-10 increase, 93.43→93.54%, and lower means otherwise: 72.37→71.61%, 91.75→91.59%, and 57.21→56.54%. These configurations provide little evidence of a dropout benefit; comparisons were omitted from the record.
relationships.display_finding: Reported mean accuracy increased slightly for ResNet-18 on CIFAR-10 and decreased otherwise, with dropout tuning unspecified. These comparisons have not been independently checked.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: ResNet-18 and EfficientNetV2-S trained from scratch on augmented CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100
source_check.reason: Tables 1–2 show baseline-to-Dropout accuracy changes of 93.43→93.54% and 72.37→71.61% for ResNet-18, and 91.75→91.59% and 57.21→56.54% for EfficientNetV2-S. These mixed fixed-recipe results qualify the benefit without establishing failure after suitable tuning.

relationships.condition: ImageNet-1k linear probing with frozen MambaOut-Base-Plus or Swin Transformer Base features
